title: Package tests
description: A test suite the integration audit runs against the application (master plan 4.5 checks 6, 8 and 10, 9.4): synthetic fixtures for a disposable tenant, positive and negative scope probes, safe-execution probes for every consequential operation, optional conversation cases and a runtime smoke test. One or more files under tests/. Everything here is test-only and synthetic: no real tenant, person or record belongs in a package, and nothing here is ever used at runtime. The suite declares WHAT to probe and what outcome is correct; AlixAI's audit executes it deterministically and records the result. The schema fixes the shape and the two things that must exist (a positive and a negative scope probe, a text smoke path); that every capability is covered is the loader's and the audit's check. Authored as YAML; this schema validates the parsed JSON form.

suite.description: The suite ID, unique in the package.

description.description: Optional note on what the suite covers.

synthetic.description: Always true. States that every tenant, principal and record in the suite is synthetic and privacy-safe.

fixtures.description: The disposable tenants, principals and records the probes use, and the application operations that create and remove them.

scope_probes.description: Positive and negative scope probes (master plan 4.5 check 6). At least one probe must expect allow and at least one must expect deny: a suite that only checks what works proves nothing about isolation. A denied probe passes only if the unauthorized record or chunk never reaches the model.

safety_probes.description: Safe-execution probes (master plan 4.5 check 8): prepare/confirm/commit, idempotency, expiry, cancellation, stale-record invalidation and uncertain-response recovery. Every consequential operation (risk level 1 or higher) needs probes of every kind; the loader and the audit check coverage. May be empty only for an application with read-only capabilities.

conversation_cases.description: Optional multi-turn conversation cases for the conversation test harness. Test-only: expectations are checked against deterministic results, never used as runtime policy.

smoke.description: The runtime smoke test against a disposable tenant (master plan 4.5 check 10).

provisioning.description: The application operations that create and remove the synthetic data.

tenants.description: The disposable tenants, by logical reference. At least two, so cross-tenant probes exist. The references are logical names: the audit generates the real tenant and workspace IDs for the disposable run.

ref.description: Logical tenant reference, unique in the suite.

workspaces.description: Logical references of the tenant's workspaces. At least one.

principals.description: The synthetic principals, by logical reference. At least two, so cross-principal probes exist.

records.description: The synthetic records the seed operation creates, by logical reference. At least one.

create_tenant.description: The inspection or management operation that creates a disposable tenant with its workspaces and principals.

seed.description: The operation that loads the synthetic records.

cleanup.description: The operation that removes the disposable tenant and everything the run created. The smoke test verifies nothing is left.

seed_data.description: Optional package-relative path (below tests/) of the synthetic data file the seed operation reads.

ref.description: Logical principal reference, unique in the suite.

tenant.description: The reference of one of the fixture tenants.

workspace.description: The reference of one of that tenant's workspaces.

roles.description: Roles the principal's context carries. Each must be declared in the manifest's tenancy.roles. At least one.

ref.description: Logical record reference, unique in the suite.

entity_type.description: The entity type of the record.

tenant.description: The fixture tenant the record belongs to.

workspace.description: The fixture workspace the record belongs to.

id.description: Probe ID, unique in the suite.

dimension.description: The scope boundary the probe tests (master plan 4.5 check 6): tenant, workspace, principal, role, record, document or source.

operation.description: What is attempted: a capability operation (read, validate, prepare, commit, status) or retrieve, a RAG retrieval.

capability_id.description: The capability attempted. Required for every operation except retrieve.

principal.description: The reference of the fixture principal making the attempt.

target_record.description: The reference of the fixture record the attempt targets, for record-level probes.

target_source.description: The ID of the RAG source retrieved from, for source and document probes.

expect.description: allow: the attempt succeeds. deny: it is refused with error_code, and nothing about the target is disclosed.

error_code.description: The error code a denied attempt must produce. Required for deny, not allowed for allow.

id.description: Probe ID, unique in the suite.

principal.description: The reference of the fixture principal acting.

kind.description: confirmed_commit: prepare, confirm, commit once. unconfirmed_commit: commit without the required confirmation. replayed_commit: the same commit sent twice. expired_preparation: commit after the preparation expired. stale_record: a record changes between prepare and commit. cancelled_preparation: commit after cancellation. uncertain_commit_recovery: the commit response is lost, and status decides whether to retry.

outcome.description: committed_once: the effect was applied exactly once. rejected_no_effect: the attempt failed with error_code and changed nothing. original_receipt_returned: a repeat returned the first receipt and changed nothing more. recovered_via_status: status established what happened and the action was neither lost nor duplicated.

error_code.description: The error code of a rejected attempt. Required for rejected_no_effect, not allowed otherwise.

id.description: Case ID, unique in the suite.

language.description: The language of the user turns.

capability_id.description: The capability the conversation is about.

principal.description: The reference of the fixture principal talking.

turns.description: The user turns in order, each with what the controller must do. At least one.

user.description: What the user says in this turn.

act.description: The dialogue act of the resulting DialogueDirective (the vocabulary is defined by the conversation object schemas, docs/integration/conversation-objects.md), for example ask_missing, disambiguate, request_confirmation, request_step_up, report_outcome or report_failure. The generated act enum is the vocabulary; the alias ask_missing_field is still accepted and read as ask_missing.

missing_fields.description: The fields the controller must report as missing.

fields.description: Field values the controller must hold after the turn.

error_code.description: The error code the turn must produce, for a failing turn.

paths.description: The end-to-end paths exercised in the disposable tenant. A text path is required; voice, rag and action paths are listed when the application has them.

verify_cleanup.description: Always true. After the run the audit verifies that the disposable tenant and every record the run created are gone.

id.description: Path ID, unique in the suite.

path.description: text, voice (a synthetic transcript), rag (a question answered from a source) or action (a prepare, confirm, commit round trip).

principal.description: The reference of the fixture principal.

capability_id.description: The capability exercised. Required for the action path.

utterance.description: What the synthetic user says or asks.

audit_events.description: The audit event types the path must produce, so the audit trail is exercised along with the behaviour. At least one.

citations.description: For the rag path: true if the answer must carry original-source citations, false if the path must return no_supported_evidence.
